title: Do electricians in Queensland need annual CPR and rescue training?
description: Queensland rescue and resuscitation rules for electrical workers under the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026: safety observers, licence renewal and evidence.
shortAnswer: Yes, in practice. Queensland's Electrical Safety Regulation 2026, which replaced the 2013 Regulation on September 1, 2026, requires businesses to ensure workers who perform electrical work are competent in rescue and resuscitation, requires a safety observer assessed in the previous 12 months for energized work, and makes continued resuscitation competence a condition of licence renewal. The Electrical Safety Office expects CPR refresher training within 12 months before renewal.
keyTakeaways: The Electrical Safety Regulation 2013 (Qld) expired on August 31, 2026 under staged repeal. The Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 commenced on September 1, 2026, so older section references (such as section 28) are now out of date.

Section 211 requires a business to ensure workers who perform or help perform electrical work are competent in rescue and resuscitation "in accordance with recognised practices in the electricity industry", with a maximum penalty of 40 penalty units.
The 12 month rule is in the definition of safety observer in Schedule 10: the observer must have been assessed in the previous 12 months as competent to rescue and resuscitate a person.
To renew an electrical work licence, section 167 requires the holder to continue to satisfy the resuscitation requirement, and linespersons the pole top or tower rescue requirement.
The Electrical Safety Office says CPR refresher training, and pole top rescue for linespersons, must be completed within twelve months of renewal, and certificates may be requested later for audit.
regulator: Electrical Safety Office, Office of Industrial Relations (Workplace Health and Safety Queensland), administering the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) and the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld)
appliesTo: Persons conducting a business or undertaking (PCBUs) whose workers perform or help perform electrical work in Queensland
Holders of electrical mechanic, fitter, linesperson, jointer and restricted electrical work licences
Safety observers for electrical work on or near energized electrical equipment
Employers and supervisors of electrical apprentices and trainees

sections.heading: Which Queensland regulation sets the rescue and resuscitation rules?

blocks.text: Since September 1, 2026 the rules are in the [Electrical Safety Regulation 2026](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2026-0113), made under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld). The [Electrical Safety Regulation 2013](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/repealed/current/sl-2013-0213) reached the end of its postponed staged repeal date on August 31, 2026 and is no longer in force.

According to [WorkSafe Queensland](https://www.worksafe.qld.gov.au/laws-and-compliance/electrical-safety-laws/electrical-safety-regulation-2026), the 2026 Regulation "does not introduce new policy or regulatory obligations". It reorders and regroups the provisions. The practical effect for training managers is that the substance is unchanged but the section numbers are not: the general rescue and resuscitation duty that sat in section 28 of the 2013 Regulation is now section 211, and the licensing provisions have moved into Part 7.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) as in force at commencement and Electrical Safety Office guidance, as at November 2026. Policies, SWMS templates and training matrices that cite 2013 Regulation section numbers should be updated.

sections.heading: What does section 211 require of employers?

blocks.text: Section 211 requires a PCBU to ensure that workers who are required to perform, or help in performing, electrical work are competent in rescue and resuscitation in accordance with recognized practices in the electricity industry. The maximum penalty is 40 penalty units. The duty covers helpers and trade assistants, not only licence holders.

The section does not name a course, a unit of competency or a fixed interval. The standard is competence measured against "recognised practices in the electricity industry". That is why the industry treats annual CPR and low voltage rescue refreshers as the baseline: the 12 month assessment period written into the safety observer definition, and the Electrical Safety Office's 12 month expectation for licence renewal, are the clearest published benchmarks of what recognized practice means in Queensland.

Section 211(2) gives one exception. The duty does not apply to a worker whose electrical work licence carries a condition that they must not act in a role requiring rescue and resuscitation competence, including as a safety observer. That condition is how the regulator accommodates a medical condition that prevents someone performing CPR.

sections.heading: Where does the 12 month assessment requirement come from?

blocks.text: It comes from the definition of safety observer in Schedule 10 of the 2026 Regulation. A safety observer for electrical work must be competent to implement control measures in an emergency, competent to rescue and resuscitate the worker if necessary, and must have been "assessed in the previous 12 months as competent to rescue and resuscitate a person".

Section 203 then makes the safety observer mandatory for most energized work. A PCBU must ensure electrical work on or near energized electrical equipment is performed by a competent person with suitable, tested tools and personal protective equipment, under a safe work method statement, and observed by a safety observer. The maximum penalty is 60 penalty units. A safety observer is not required only where the work consists solely of testing and the risk assessment shows no serious risk.

The [Managing electrical risks in the workplace Code of Practice 2021](https://www.worksafe.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0025/72637/managing-electrical-risks-in-the-workplace-cop-2021.pdf) repeats the 12 month assessment rule and adds practical expectations: the observer should not be given other tasks that compromise the role, should not be in the elevating work platform basket with the worker, and must be able to communicate quickly with the person doing the work. The code lists "electrical rescue and resuscitation training for safety observers" among the training a PCBU should provide.

sections.heading: How does rescue and resuscitation affect getting and renewing a licence?

blocks.text: Resuscitation competence is an eligibility requirement for both issue and renewal. Under section 155, the regulator must be satisfied that an applicant has been trained in, and is competent to carry out, resuscitation on an individual who has stopped breathing or is unconscious because of electric shock. Applicants for an electrical linesperson licence must also be trained and competent in rescue from a pole top or transmission tower.

Section 167 applies the same test at renewal and reinstatement: the holder must continue to satisfy the resuscitation requirement and, for linespersons, the rescue requirement. Under section 170 an electrical work licence may be renewed or reinstated for a maximum of 5 years.

The [Electrical Safety Office's renewal page](https://www.worksafe.qld.gov.au/licensing-and-registrations/electrical-licences/electrical-worker-licences/renew-or-reinstate-your-electrical-work-licence) translates this into a timing rule: CPR refresher training within twelve months of renewal, and pole top or transmission tower rescue training within twelve months of renewal for linespersons. Licence holders do not upload the certificates when they renew, but "may be required to provide it at a later date for auditing purposes". A licence can be renewed up to two months before expiry and reinstated within 12 months after it expires.

sections.heading: What extra rules apply to apprentices and trainees?

blocks.text: Section 307 restricts what a PCBU may let a training person do in the first 6 months of an apprenticeship or training program. The training person must not work in the immediate vicinity of a live high voltage exposed part, or where there is a risk of contact with a live low voltage exposed part.

There is a narrow exception for acting as a safety observer: the training person must have been capable of being a safety observer for at least 1 year before the apprenticeship started, and the PCBU must keep a written record of the 12 month rescue and resuscitation assessment for that person. Every training person who performs electrical work must be supervised at all times by a licensed electrical worker licensed for that work.

blocks.text: Two gaps appear repeatedly in audits. First, the renewal timing belongs to the individual and the observer timing belongs to the job, so a worker can be compliant for licence purposes but out of date as an observer. Second, helpers are covered by section 211 even though they hold no licence. A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) that tracks expiry per person per role, and a [refresh cycle](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) set at 12 months for both CPR and rescue, closes both.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records rescue and resuscitation as a role level competency with a 12 month validity, linked to the safety observer role and to each licence class, so expiry can be checked against the job on the day rather than the licence date. The same structure supports [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) on site specific rescue kits. See how this applies to [energy and resources organizations](/industries/energy-resources).

faqs.q: Does the Regulation actually use the words low voltage rescue?
faqs.a: No. The Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 uses "rescue and resuscitation" and, for linespersons, rescue from a pole top or transmission tower. Low voltage rescue is the industry name for the rescue component most electricians train in, and is how most providers package the training that meets the section 211 and safety observer requirements.

faqs.q: Is section 28 still the right reference for rescue and resuscitation training in Queensland?
faqs.a: Not after August 31, 2026. Section 28 was the provision in the Electrical Safety Regulation 2013, which expired under staged repeal. The equivalent duty is section 211 of the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026, with the same wording and the same 40 penalty unit maximum.

faqs.q: What if a worker has a medical condition that prevents them performing CPR?
faqs.a: The regulator can still issue or renew the licence if the condition does not otherwise affect the person's ability to do electrical work, with a condition that they must not act in a role requiring rescue and resuscitation competence, such as safety observer. Section 211 then does not apply to that worker.

faqs.q: Do I need to send my CPR certificate when renewing an electrical licence online?
faqs.a: No. The Electrical Safety Office says licence holders are not required to provide copies of CPR, pole top rescue or skills maintenance certificates at renewal, but may be asked for them later for audit. Keep the certificates for the full licence cycle.

factCheck.claim: The Electrical Safety Regulation 2013 (SL 2013 No. 213) was repealed by staged repeal on 31 August 2026 (postponed from 1 September 2024)
The Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 commences on 1 September 2026 (section 2) and replaces the 2013 Regulation without new policy or regulatory obligations

Section 211 requires a PCBU to ensure workers who perform or help perform electrical work are competent in rescue and resuscitation in accordance with recognised practices in the electricity industry; maximum penalty 40 penalty units; s 211(2) licence condition exception. Same wording was s 28 of the 2013 Regulation

Schedule 10 defines safety observer as a person competent to implement emergency controls and rescue and resuscitate, who has been assessed in the previous 12 months as competent to rescue and resuscitate a person
Section 203 requires energized electrical work to be observed by a safety observer (maximum penalty 60 penalty units) except testing-only work where the risk assessment shows no serious risk

Section 155 requires applicants to be trained and competent in resuscitation for electric shock, and linespersons in pole top or transmission tower rescue; s 167 requires continued satisfaction at renewal; s 170 sets a maximum 5 year renewal term

Section 307 bars training persons in the first 6 months from working near live HV exposed parts or where there is a risk of contact with live LV exposed parts, with a safety observer exception requiring 1 year prior capability and a written record of the assessment

ESO requires CPR refresher training within twelve months of renewal and PTR within twelve months for linespersons; certificates not required at renewal but may be required for audit; renew up to two months before expiry; reinstate within 12 months

The Managing electrical risks in the workplace Code of Practice 2021 lists electrical rescue and resuscitation training for safety observers and states the safety observer should not be in the EWP basket
